audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Zacchaeus, salvation to Abraham's son, minas parable, Jerusalem entry, lament over city, and temple action.

verses.restored: Entering, he was passing through Jericho.

familiar.text: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.

verses.restored: Look, a man called by name Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

familiar.text: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.

verses.restored: He was seeking to see who Jesus was, and he was not able because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.

familiar.text: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.

verses.restored: Running ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore fig tree so that he might see him, because he was about to pass that way.

familiar.text: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.

verses.restored: When Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today it is necessary for me to remain in your house.

familiar.text: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

verses.restored: He hurried, came down, and received him rejoicing.

familiar.text: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.

verses.restored: Seeing this, all were grumbling, saying, He went in to lodge with a sinful/misaligned man.

familiar.text: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.

verses.restored: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, Look, half of my possessions, Lord, I give to the poor; and if I extorted anything from anyone, I restore fourfold.

familiar.text: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

verses.restored: For the Son of Humanity came to seek and to save/heal the lost.

familiar.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

verses.restored: As they were hearing these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought the reign of the Divine was about to appear immediately.

familiar.text: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.

verses.restored: He said, A certain noble person went into a far country to receive a reign for himself and return.

familiar.text: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

verses.restored: Calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them, Do business until I come.

familiar.text: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

verses.restored: But his citizens hated him and sent an embassy after him, saying, We do not want this one to reign over us.

familiar.text: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

verses.restored: It happened when he returned, having received the reign, he ordered these servants to whom he had given the silver to be called, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.

verses.restored: The first came, saying, Lord, your mina made ten more minas.

familiar.text: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

verses.restored: He said to him, Well done, good servant; because you were trustworthy in a very little thing, have authority over ten cities.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

verses.restored: The second came, saying, Your mina, Lord, made five minas.

familiar.text: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.

verses.restored: He said also to this one, And you, be over five cities.

familiar.text: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.

verses.restored: Another came, saying, Lord, look, your mina, which I kept laid away in a cloth.

familiar.text: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:

verses.restored: For I feared you, because you are a severe person; you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.

familiar.text: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.

verses.restored: He says to him, From your own mouth I will judge you, harmful servant. You knew that I am a severe person, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?

familiar.text: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:

verses.restored: Why then did you not give my silver to the bank, and I, coming, would have collected it with interest?

familiar.text: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?

verses.restored: He said to those standing by, Take the mina from him and give it to the one having ten minas.

familiar.text: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.

verses.restored: They said to him, Lord, he has ten minas.

familiar.text: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)

verses.restored: I say to you that to everyone having, more will be given; but from the one not having, even what one has will be taken.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.

verses.restored: But these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me.

familiar.text: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.

verses.restored: After saying these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem.

verses.restored: It happened, as he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mountain called Olivet, he sent two of the disciples,

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,

verses.restored: saying, Go into the opposite village, in which entering you will find a colt tied, on which no human has ever sat. Loose it and bring it.

familiar.text: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.

verses.restored: If anyone asks you, Why are you loosing it? you shall say this: The Lord has need of it.

familiar.text: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.

verses.restored: Those sent went away and found just as he had said to them.

familiar.text: And they that were sent went their way, and found even as he had said unto them.

verses.restored: As they were loosing the colt, its lords said to them, Why are you loosing the colt?

familiar.text: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?

verses.restored: They said, The Lord has need of it.

familiar.text: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.

verses.restored: They brought it to Jesus, and throwing their garments on the colt, they set Jesus on it.

familiar.text: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus thereon.

verses.restored: As he went, they were spreading their garments on the way.

familiar.text: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.

verses.restored: As he was already drawing near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began rejoicing to praise the Divine with a great voice for all the powers they had seen,

familiar.text: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;

verses.restored: saying, Blessed is the coming king in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.

familiar.text: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.

verses.restored: Some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, Teacher, rebuke your disciples.

familiar.text: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.

verses.restored: Answering, he said, I say to you, if these are silent, the stones will cry out.

familiar.text: And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.

verses.restored: As he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it,

familiar.text: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,

verses.restored: saying, If you had known in this day, even you, the things for peace; but now they have been hidden from your eyes.

familiar.text: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

verses.restored: For days will come upon you when your enemies will throw up a barricade around you, surround you, and press you in on every side.

familiar.text: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,

verses.restored: They will dash you and your children within you to the ground, and they will not leave stone upon stone in you, because you did not know the time of your visitation.

familiar.text: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

verses.restored: Entering the temple, he began to cast out those selling,

familiar.text: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;

verses.restored: saying to them, It has been written, My house will be a house of prayer, but you made it a cave of robbers.

familiar.text: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.

verses.restored: He was teaching daily in the temple. The chief priests, scribes, and first people of the people were seeking to destroy him,

familiar.text: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,

verses.restored: but they were not finding what they might do, for all the people were hanging upon him, listening.

familiar.text: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.
